stemMd: A council should not cancel the mobile library merely because its cost per loan is high. Its purpose is to reach people unable to visit a branch, and the branch libraries cannot serve those people at any cost. The statement about branch libraries chiefly

options.label: A
options.textMd: explains why an ordinary cost-per-loan comparison overlooks the service's distinctive benefit.

options.label: B
options.textMd: denies that the mobile service is expensive per loan.

options.label: C
options.textMd: shows that all readers prefer mobile services.

options.label: D
options.textMd: establishes that branch libraries should close.

options.label: E
options.textMd: proves that the mobile library has no operating costs.

explanationMd: A metric useful for interchangeable services can mislead when one service reaches otherwise excluded users. The branch limitation explains why the mobile library's cost cannot be assessed solely against ordinary branch loans.

distractorRationale.d: The conclusion concerns retaining a different service.
distractorRationale.c: Preference is not the issue; access is.
distractorRationale.e: The argument compares benefits, not costlessness.
distractorRationale.b: The argument can concede that expense.
